intro: You've searched for a retirement planner near you, which usually means you want to understand your options and speak to someone face to face about your pension and retirement plans. Retirement planners map your goals, model your income and recommend steps to help you retire on your terms. iComply can introduce you to a suitable UK pension adviser who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a retirement planner near them usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for a retirement planner near them want clear, local advice on turning their pension savings into a reliable income.
needs: You want to know how much income your pension pot could realistically provide and whether it will last as long as you need.
You are approaching retirement and need help deciding when to start drawing on your pension and how to take it tax-efficiently.
You have several pension pots from different jobs and want to understand whether consolidating them makes sense for you.
You are unsure how inflation will affect your retirement income and want a plan that takes rising costs into account.
You have a defined benefit or final salary pension and need to understand your options, including whether transferring is ever appropriate.
context: Financial advice in the UK is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). You can check that any adviser or firm is authorised, or is an appointed representative of an authorised firm, on the FCA register. If something goes wrong, you can complain to the firm and then to the Financial Ombudsman Service, and the Financial Services Compensation Scheme may protect you if an authorised firm fails.

Some pension decisions carry special rules. Advice on transferring out of a defined benefit (final salary) scheme above a set value must come from an adviser with pension transfer specialist permissions, and safeguarded benefits deserve particular care. Free, impartial guidance is also available from Pension Wise for people who have reached the age when it applies and have defined contribution pensions.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Mention that you are looking for a retirement planner near you and say which town or area you would like them to be based in or cover.
Give a rough idea of the pension pots you hold, including whether any are defined benefit or final salary schemes, without stating exact figures.
Explain what you want from retirement planning, such as checking if you can afford to retire, understanding drawdown or planning to consolidate pensions.
Say whether you have already taken any pension advice or guidance, such as from Pension Wise, so the adviser knows your starting point.
Include your preferred way of working, whether that is face to face locally, by phone or online, and any accessibility needs.
Note any deadlines you are working towards, such as a planned retirement date, so the adviser can prioritise accordingly.
questions: Are you and your firm authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority, and what permissions do you hold for pension advice?
How do you charge for retirement planning, and will I receive a clear quote before any work begins?
What experience do you have with the type of pension I hold, especially if it is a defined benefit or final salary scheme?
How will you model my retirement income and take inflation into account over the long term?
What ongoing service do you provide after the initial plan, and how is that paid for?
Will you put your recommendations in writing, including the risks and alternatives I should consider?

faqs.q: Do I need a retirement planner near me, or can I use someone further away?
faqs.a: Many people prefer a local retirement planner for face-to-face meetings, but advice can also be given by phone or online. What matters most is that the adviser is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority and that you feel comfortable with how they work.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a retirement planner and a pension adviser?
faqs.a: The terms are often used interchangeably for professionals who help you plan your retirement income and make pension decisions. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK pension adviser who will quote you directly, with fees on application.

faqs.q: Can a retirement planner help if I have a final salary pension?
faqs.a: Yes, but advice on transferring out of a defined benefit (final salary) scheme above a set value must come from an adviser with pension transfer specialist permissions. Make sure you tell iComply if you hold this type of pension so they can introduce you appropriately.

faqs.q: What free guidance is available before I see a retirement planner?
faqs.a: Pension Wise offers free, impartial guidance for people who have reached the age when it applies and have defined contribution pensions. It can help you understand your options before you speak to a financial adviser.

extra: Searching for a retirement planner near you suggests you would value meeting someone in person, perhaps at an office you can reach without a long journey. It is worth asking each planner you consider how they would hold meetings, since some work mainly by phone or video even when their office is local to you. Think about what 'near' means in practice for you, whether that is a short drive, a train ride or somewhere you can reach on foot.

When you compare retirement planners, ask what they would actually do for you: how they would map your goals, model your income and account for inflation over the years ahead. Ask too how they charge, since some work on a fixed fee and others on a percentage, and a clear quote before any work begins helps you judge whether the cost feels fair for the work involved. You can check each firm's entry on the FCA register to confirm it is authorised for pension advice.

It also helps to think about what you want from the first meeting. A retirement planner will usually want to understand your pension pots, your target income and when you hope to stop working, so gathering those details beforehand makes the conversation more useful. If you hold a final salary scheme or safeguarded benefits, mention this early, as those decisions carry special rules and may need an adviser with pension transfer specialist permissions.

extra_faqs.q: How can I judge whether a local retirement planner is right for me?
extra_faqs.a: There is no single best choice, so it helps to compare how each planner explains your options, how they charge and whether their way of working suits you. Check that the firm is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority, and ask for recommendations and risks in writing before you decide.

extra_faqs.q: Should I see a retirement planner before or after taking free guidance?
extra_faqs.a: Many people find it useful to speak to Pension Wise first if they have defined contribution pensions and have reached the age when it applies, as the free, impartial guidance can help you understand your options. You can then bring what you have learned to a retirement planner, who can give personal advice on your circumstances.
